title: Micro-fragment healing notes for label cleanup
content:
Notes-to-self: micro-fragment healing is the name I'm using for a set of heuristics that try to automatically join broken spans / fragmented entity tokens produced by upstream tokenization or noisy OCR before final label adjudication. This doc is a personal sandbox for examples, quick heuristics, and potential checks to add into the curation pipeline.

Problem statement:
- We keep seeing short fragments of the same logical entity separated by punctuation or tokenization artifacts. Example types: hyphenation splits, mid-string punctuation ("/", "|"), embedded markup tags, soft line breaks, and OCR mis-segmentation.
- Current heuristics treat each fragment as an independent candidate which increases false negatives for entity recall and inflates manual adjudication load.

Goals:
- Define conservative rules that boost recall without creating many false positive merges.
- Produce small, auditable candidate merges with a confidence score so labelers can accept/reject quickly.
- Keep the approach explainable and reversible (easy to rollback).

Heuristics (first pass, conservative):
1) Adjacent short-fragment joiner:
   - If two adjacent tokens/spans are both length <= 6 characters and combined length <= 20, and join char is one of ["-", "/", "|", ","], consider as join candidate.
   - Require that combined token matches an entity lexicon or detects capitalization pattern that suggests single proper noun (e.g., "Acme-" + "Corp" -> "Acme-Corp").

2) Linebreak / hyphen recovery (OCR prone):
   - If token ends with a hyphen at end-of-line and next line token starts with lowercase or capitalized continuation, merge and strip hyphen.
   - Only apply if original context shows no additional punctuation between lines.

3) Embedded markup stripper then merge:
   - Remove lightweight markup artifacts before span comparison (common: <i>, [sic], ®, ™). If removing markup makes two spans identical or adjacent, create candidate merge.

4) Fuzzy overlap coalescer:
   - When two spans overlap or sit with <=1 char gap and edit distance normalized by length <= 0.2, suggest coalesce with backoff to preserve longer span.

5) Numeric and SKU rules (special-case):
   - For short numeric fragments separated by non-alphanumerics but share a prefix/suffix pattern (e.g., "123-456" split into "123" and "456"), only auto-merge if pattern matches product SKU regex OR appears >5x in the dataset in same split form.

Candidate scoring (simple features to surface to labeler):
- combined_length (smaller = lower risk),
- lexicon_match (boolean),
- punctuation_strength (how strong the separator is; comma weaker, hyphen stronger),
- dataset_frequency_of_combined_form (high frequency = high score),
- ocr_confidence_bucket (low OCR confidence -> increase score threshold).

Quick acceptance UI idea:
- Show 3 context snippets where merge occurs (left/center/right), show original spans highlighted, suggested merged form, candidate score, and a one-click accept / reject. Keep accept rate metrics.

Examples (concrete):
1) "Acme-\nCorp" (OCR line break) -> candidate: "Acme-Corp"; lexicon_match true -> auto-suggest high.
2) "bio/chem" labeled as tag vs entity: separator "/" ambiguous. Candidate: join if both sides capitalized or present in company list. Else defer.
3) "Q5|B2" -> likely separate fields (do not merge) unless domain list says combined SKU exists.
4) "St. Louis" sometimes tokenized into ["St.", "Louis"]; join rule should prefer preserving punctuation and standard canonicalization to "St. Louis".

Adjudication heuristics (labeler TOOLS):
- If candidate score > .85 and lexicon_match true -> show auto-check option (auto-accept into pipeline with daily audit).
- Scores between .5 and .85 -> queue for quick human review (1-click).
- Scores < .5 -> only used for downstream fuzzy matching, do not change labels automatically.

Sampling plan for manual checks:
- Weekly random sample of 250 auto-merged items (stratified by score buckets) for QA.
- Track precision by bucket; target > 98% precision for auto-accept bucket, >90% for quick-review accept decisions.

Edge-cases and notes: 
- Multi-language: hyphenation rules differ (German compound words vs English). Add language-aware backoff.
- Person names with initials: "J. R. R." merging rules are different; avoid aggressive joining there.
- Legal names with punctuation (O'Neil, D'Angelo) should not be split-merged incorrectly. Use apostrophe whitelist.

Small prototype plan (2-week sprint):
- Week 1: implement three rules (adjacent short-fragment joiner, hyphen recovery, markup stripper) + scoring pipeline. Add flagging in labeling UI.
- Week 2: collect feedback, build sampling QA dashboard, tune thresholds, add SKU exceptions.

Action items (me / next steps):
- [ ] Draft small PR for data-tools: add candidate generator endpoint (Diego assigned).
- [ ] Add lightweight lexicon of high-confidence company/product names (Ayesha to export from product taxonomy).
- [ ] Wire sampling dashboard into QA metrics (me).
- [ ] Add language detection probe to decide language-specific backoffs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Where do we store canonical "merged" forms? In label metadata as "merged_from"? Need schema change discussions with infra.
- How often to run automatic healing vs on ingest? Real-time may be expensive; offline batch might be more stable.
- Should merged candidates be reversible on downstream labels rollback? Need explicit audit trail.

Quick reference examples for labelers (paste into UI hint):
- Accept candidate: "Acme-Corp" (Acme- + Corp across linebreak).
- Reject candidate: "Q5|B2" (two distinct fields).
- Defer: "bio/chem" unless appears in lexicon.

Notes-to-self (style): keep heuristics conservative at first. Prefer more manual review than silent incorrect merges. Write short unit tests that show the merge candidates in small synthetic cases.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate once we have initial precision numbers from sampling.

Unresolved: add short JSONL export example to test harness for Diego. Will create a separate note for that export mechanics.
